Brand proposal · Sep 2026

The first sport that scores your head.

Every sport in the world scores what your body did. We score what was left of you while it did it, and turn that into a number you can chase and lose.

Decision racingthe category we create
Head goes before legsthe person we build for
Composurethe feeling we own
The Deltathe asset nobody else has

01 · The idea

One number, and nobody else can show it.

The memo already builds it. Forty-five minutes, five stations, a physical demand and a cognitive demand running at the same time, and a score at the end.

The brand is the number that comes out of it, and specifically the part of that number that measures deterioration.

The brand platform

The Delta

One line: how much of your judgement survives the effort

CHALLENGE → MEASURE → UNDERSTAND THE GAP → TRAIN WITH PURPOSE → IMPROVE YOUR SCORE

That line is the memo's own, from its section 02, and the idea inside it is the whole sport. The body drops eight per cent under load and the head drops nineteen, and nobody else in fitness takes that second number. The distance is the delta, and closing it is the entire sport.

HYROX shows a time · Whoop shows a strain · Lumosity shows a streak · SPARKD shows a wellness score · Nobody shows what you lost

Comment on the name of the metricDes · 10 Sep

The memo calls this the gap. The line quoted above is the memo's own and the idea inside it is right, so what moves here is the label and nothing under it.

In Spain the word is taken. GAP is a class on every gym timetable, glúteos, abdominales y piernas, and the first club opens in Madrid, so the term would arrive attached to somebody else's product and to an audience this sport is not built for. It reads clean in English, which is why it survived the memo, and it stops the first time a coach says it out loud in a Spanish gym.

Delta is the same word in Spanish and English, and it has meant the difference between two measurements for a century. It also arrives with a mark, Δ, that nothing in the category is using.

The cost is real. Gap needs no explaining and delta needs half a sentence, paid at the first visit, which is why the score card in section 09 carries the definition under the number. Worth settling now, because the price of moving the word climbs the moment it goes on a wall.

How the number is made

Two measurements, and the delta is the distance between them. An athlete runs at a set pace with nothing to think about, then answers the signals standing still, and those are the baselines. Then both happen at once, and both scores fall, because attention is finite.

SystemAloneBoth at onceWhat it gave up
Physicalbaseline868.7% of itself, to share the room
Cognitivebaseline8219.3%. This is the delta

Because it is a ratio against an athlete's own baseline, a thirty-year-old and a fifty-five-year-old can hold the same delta and mean the same thing by it. It is also the only number in fitness anybody wants to get smaller, which the brand gets for free.

The rule that has to travel with it. The physical demand has to be prescribed rather than chosen. If athletes set their own pace the way to win is to jog, because at a slow enough effort thinking barely suffers and the delta looks superb. A delta only means anything at a fixed intensity, so that goes in the rulebook in version one. It also makes the first visit a baseline test, which is the practical case for selling the test rather than the class.

One number too many. Section 03 of the memo carries an Integration subscore of 77, described as how well the athlete did both at once, which is the question the delta answers. Two numbers competing to be the point leaves neither as the point, so one goes, and the delta is the one with a name people can say out loud.

02 · The belief

Everything that goes wrong goes wrong while you are tired.

The moments that cost people something happen at the end of a shift, in the last ten minutes of a match, on the drive home, in the fourth hour of a hard day, and that is where this sport lives.

Fifty years of fitness has trained the body and left the head to look after itself.

Where the belief comes from

Founder

A founder who has not enjoyed training since rugby, tried CrossFit, and two months ago found dual training and has not stopped. A sport founded by someone who went looking for it has a true story, which is the cheapest marketing there is.

Why it matters now

Cultural

The argument from the voice note: the more we hand over to machines, the less we practise deciding. It gets louder every year for the next decade, and this sport is placed to catch it. Say it once and let it sit.

The north star

The Games, 2040.

The original Games were built on one idea, that a complete person trains body and mind as a single thing, and the Greek word for it was arete. Modern sport split them and spent a century scoring the half it could time. A sport that scores both is a return to the original brief, and pointing it at the Games is ambitious and correct.

A north star is a standard, and this one is demanding. It asks for a number comparable across countries before it is comparable across gyms, rules written down and enforced, a governing body before there is much to govern, and a format somebody would sit and watch. Each is a constraint worth welcoming, because each makes the sport more real.

A real athlete is both mind and body · A standard, held daily · Fourteen years, planned

The discipline. The belief carries the brand and the science carries the credibility, in that order, because leading with decline lowers the price and brings the wrong first hundred people.

03 · The category

Create the category, then win it.

“Fitness racing” did not exist as a phrase before HYROX wrote it down. By 2026 Puma and Adidas are fighting inside a category one company named.

The category name ends up worth more than the brand name, because it is the words everybody else has to borrow.

Decision racing

Recommended

Puts the sport's real subject in the category name. “I race decisions” is a sentence somebody repeats at a dinner table, which is the whole test.

Load racing

Alternative

Says physical and cognitive load in one word and sits naturally beside fitness racing. Reads gym-first, which risks underselling the half that makes this new.

Dual racing

Weakest

Closest to the science and easiest to explain to a researcher. It is half a step from “dual-task”, which is laboratory language and belongs in the appendix.

What to retire on day one. “Cognitive-motor performance” and “brain-body training” file the brand next to Lumosity, BrainHQ and Muse, a category whose credibility problem the memo describes on page two. The science underneath stays.

04 · Who it is for

One person, chosen so everyone else overhears it.

The memo says the 8-year-old, the 43-year-old worker and the 62-year-old. All three will eventually be right.

None of them makes a brand, because a brand gets built for one person and the rest overhear it.

The one we build for

Core

Profile: 40, already races, already measures

They have a PB they are proud of, and somewhere in the last third of a race they have noticed their decisions go before their legs do. They have felt this and have no name for it, so nobody has to explain the product to them.

They already buy: HYROX, races, a coach, a watch

Who it is not for, yet

Later

The person looking for a gentler gym. The person sent by a doctor. The corporate wellness buyer, a different person from the founder who books a team session in section 11.

Real markets, all of them, and cheaper to reach in year three

Their real anxiety. The athlete above has watched three fitness fads come and go since university, so the first question is whether this is CrossFit with flashing lights. The answer is the retest: twenty athletes, a baseline and a second number. Put that proof in front, because nothing else settles it.

05 · The position

The sport of deciding tired.

HYROX asks how fast you finished. We ask how much of you was still there at minute thirty-eight, with four stations behind you and the rule just changed.

Positioning statement

For athletes who already measure themselves, we are the sport that scores judgement under load, because strength you cannot use when it matters is decoration.

Owns the word delta · Owns the category decision racing · Owns the feeling composure

The shape of it

Four things, three of them in order and each earning the next, and one that runs alongside from the first month.

A club in Madrid

One room where the delta gets measured properly for the first time and the first hundred athletes get their first number. A club that is only a test is a laboratory, so it is also where people stay afterwards. Somebody enters for the test and comes back for the people.

Earns the number, and the crowd

HYROX owns no gyms and CrossFit owns no boxes, and both make their money certifying other people's rooms and owning the standard. The condition comes before the contract, which is that a delta measured in Valencia means what it means in Madrid, or the licence is selling a class.

It is a direction, and section 02 says why. A sport pointed at the Games has to write its rules down, make its number comparable across countries, and be worth watching. Those are design constraints, and good ones to have early.

The app, at home

Alongside
OrderFrom month one
WhereHome
NeedsA watch, and a baseline

Where the delta history lives, and where somebody practises on a Tuesday night with a watch on. Load is prescribed by heart-rate zone, so the intensity rule survives the living room, and a home number is practice, in lowercase, because only a test in a certified room records one. It opens after a baseline in Madrid, and where it gets used most is where the next room goes.

Keeps the number moving between sessions

What we give up to hold it

  • The health story, which is the one with the science and the institutional doors, parked for two or three years.
  • The older athlete in the memo, who arrives later and arrives anyway.
  • Any claim to being gentle, accessible or beginner-friendly in the first wave.
  • Licensing the format before a second room can reproduce the number, however many people ask.

One commercial consequence worth taking seriously. Sell the test rather than the class. A class competes with a thousand classes in Madrid and gets priced like one. A test is something you can fail, and a number you have been given is something you want to move. The club sells the test at the door and the membership after it.

06 · The feeling

Composure is unclaimed.

Every fitness brand sells a feeling before it sells a session, and in this category two feelings are already taken. Both are crowded because they were the obvious ones.

The feeling between them is empty, and it is the one we produce.

TakenEmptyTaken
GritHYROX · Spartan · DEKASuffering as proof
ComposureNobodyJudgement that survives the effort
ReassuranceSPARKD · Lumosity · MuseProtection against decline

Grit

Taken

Sells: suffering as proof

The mud, the ice bath, the finish-line collapse, the photograph of someone destroyed. The loudest territory in fitness, and the one Puma and Adidas are arriving in, so a new sport standing there is one more voice in a full room.

Composure

Ours

Sells: the clearest head in a loud room

The feeling of still deciding well at minute thirty-eight, when the body has started to argue. It is a status feeling, rare and visible, and choosing it says something about a person that a mud run cannot. It is also the feeling the delta measures, which is why no other brand can claim it without the number.

Reassurance

Taken

Sells: protection against decline

Calm and slightly medical, spoken to people who are worried. It has the science and the institutional doors, and it caps what anyone will pay, because protection gets priced like insurance. It also brings the wrong first hundred people.

How we know it is real. Composure is already in the photography direction in section 09, where the body is blurred and the eyes are sharp and nobody poses. The feeling was in the craft before it had a name, and naming it means someone other than the founder can execute it.

07 · The name

Three things need naming, and only one of them is the brand.

Collapsing them is what makes naming feel hard. The brand gets registered and defended, so it has to be defensible. The category has to be repeatable by competitors, and the metric answers to neither rule.

A metric can be a common word, because metrics win by being said rather than owned. Par. Handicap. VO2 max. Split.

What gets namedProposalWhy this kind of word
The metricthe deltaCommon noun, and that is fine. A metric wins by being said often enough to become the unit.
The categorydecision racingDescriptive on purpose. Competitors have to use our words to explain themselves.
The brandAGONShort, hard, strange, registrable, and it reads twice. See below.

AGON

Recommended

Territory: the contest

Greek for the contest itself, the root of agony and antagonist. One syllable of struggle that sits next to HYROX and DEKA on a race listing without asking permission. Read again in English it becomes AGE ON, and the second meaning is worth more than the first.

STOA

Strong

Territory: composure

The porch in Athens where the Stoics taught that the only thing you govern is your own judgement, which is section 06 said as a name. Four letters, and it sits on a race bib next to AGON without either looking borrowed. The cleanest trademark path of the four, with the class 41 search still to run.

TELOS

Possible

Territory: the aim

The Greek word for the end a thing is built toward. For a sport whose north star sits fourteen years out it says the strategy in one word, and it reads calm and certain in both languages. It stays abstract until explained, and enough consultancies and software companies have borrowed it that the class 41 search matters more here than for STOA.

ATHLON

Possible

Territory: the athlete

The root of athlete, triathlon and decathlon, so the claim that a real athlete is mind and body sits inside the name, and it reads like a sport before anybody explains it. The cost is AMD, which sold processors under the name for twenty years to exactly this audience, and a class 41 filing does not remove the memory.

Why all four are Greek. The north star is the Games, and the Games were Greek before they were anything else. A shortlist that shares the root is a small coherence the brand gets for one decision, and it keeps the four from being unrelated short words. Only AGON carries the second reading.

The second reading

AGON. AGE ON.

The whole thesis in four letters. The sport competes now, and what it builds is the buffer that decides how somebody is doing at sixty-two. Both halves live in one word, and the brand never has to say dementia out loud to mean it.

That is the memo's tension resolved inside the name rather than parked for three years. Its section 01 argues cognitive reserve and its section 07 sells to ambitious forty-year-olds, and a name that reads two ways sells the second while quietly promising the first.

Ageing as a verb you do on purpose · Never in the tagline · Left for people to find

Two things to watch with it. The second reading only works in English, so the home market hears the Greek and the export market hears both. And it has to stay something people find rather than something the brand points at, because a forty-year-old buying a performance sport does not want ageing in the first sentence. Let it be what somebody notices in week three and tells a friend, which is the moment a name stops being a label.

On MindRock. Two syllables, hard consonants, and it lands the same in Madrid and New York. Against it: Mindrock Capital holds the trademark and the domain, rock evokes standing still while the sport rewards adapting, and compound-descriptive names explain rather than evoke. HYROX and Spartan describe nothing and are worth more than a name that tells you what is inside. It survives if there is real attachment to it, at the cost of a class 41 search and a domain that can be defended.

08 · The language

Six words the sport owns.

HYROX has the roxzone, and with one word built a vocabulary people use outside the gym, in text messages, in podcast episodes and on race day.

Owned words are what separate a sport from a class on a timetable, and they cost nothing.

ConceptWordWhy
The dual-task costthe deltaIdentical in Spanish and English, and it says itself in a bar and on a results screen.
The categoriesdelta bandsRanked by how well you hold together rather than by age. A product idea as much as a brand one.
The session at homepracticeLowercase on purpose. Practice moves your number and only a test records it, which keeps the room worth paying for.
The 500m between stationsthe transitWhere an athlete gets their head back or loses it. It earns a name because that is where the race turns.
The athleteyour number“I'm an 84.” The memo already has an athlete saying “I hit my first 85”. The loosest of the set and worth arguing about.
The roomthe agoraThe Greek gathering place, which is the social-hub brief in one word. It only works beside AGON, so it is also a small argument for AGON.

We say

Voice
  • Numbers, always. An 82 does more work than any adjective.
  • Verbs of decision: read, choose, correct, hold.
  • The failure as data. A wide delta is information about you.
  • Plain sentences. The sport is complicated enough.

We don't say

Voice
  • Brain training, brain health, cognitive-motor. Laboratory words that file us with the apps.
  • Dementia or Alzheimer's as the hook. It belongs in the science, behind the sport.
  • “There is nothing like this in the world.” SPARKD is in the memo's own bibliography.
  • Wellness, journey, mindful, recharge. Every one of them softens a thing that should be hard.

The line

The document has been avoiding a tagline, and it should stop, because three candidates are already sitting in it.

LineWhere it comes fromRead
The sport of deciding tired.Section 05Recommended. It names the behaviour, and it is a sentence somebody repeats at dinner.
The first sport that scores your head.The heroStrong. Carries the claim and the novelty, and it dates the moment there is a second one.
How much of you is left.The hero, second sentenceThe most poetic of the three, and it needs the hero sentence around it to be understood. Better as a poster than as a line under a wordmark.

09 · The look

One signal on a quiet ground.

The BlazePods in section 07 of the memo put a coloured light in the room at the moment a decision is asked for, and that hands the photography its signal for free. The room itself stays light, because the score card lives on a phone, in an email and on a wall, and a brand that only exists in the dark has one register.

One signal colour on a quiet ground, and it only ever appears where there is a measurement.

Room#080A0C
Data#F5F7FA
Signal#B8E45C
Signal on light#4E6A14

One flag on the palette. HYROX's registered colours are black, white, grey and olive #7B7100, the same hue family as this lime, in the same category, as Puma and Adidas move in. Three ways to play it: keep the lime and let the score card and the delta chart carry the distinctiveness; shift to a signal orange and keep the one-light-in-a-dark-room idea; or let the signal colour change by station, which is what the pods do, and own the behaviour of colour rather than a swatch. The third is the most interesting and the most work.

Type

SF Pro for everything read, IBM Plex Mono for clocks, scores, labels and any figure that lines up in a results table. The number is the hero, so it gets the most deliberate typography in the system: tabular figures set large, with tight tracking.

Photography

The body is blurred and the eyes are sharp, because the person is processing something, and nobody in the frame poses or smiles. If there is no light switched on for the person to answer, it is not a photograph of this sport.

Two registers, now that the club is also a place people stay. The session is the identity and the rules above are absolute inside it. The hour after is where people are allowed to be people, photographed like a good bar rather than a sport. One rule keeps the two apart: the signal colour never appears in the social register, because the signal means a measurement is happening, and on a sofa it stops meaning anything.

The photographs

The six photographs the identity is built on, with the brief each one was shot to. Two rules hold in every session frame: the lime is the only coloured light, and nobody looks at the camera.

Where the people are. Four of the six frames have more than one person in them. Keep that ratio across everything the brand publishes, because the club is the product and a lone athlete under a light does not show it.

What we never do

  • Brains, neurons, synapses, colour-coded hemispheres. The category cliché, and it files us under health.
  • Electric blue with circuitry. It says cognitive app, and it says 2016.
  • Beige and sage wellness.
  • Signal colour as a full-bleed ground, which is the point where we start looking like everyone else.
  • The app looking like an app. It inherits the score card and nothing from the store it was downloaded from.

Asset 01 · The score card, and the thing people share

Session 14 · Madrid · Open 35+ · 87th percentile

82+3
Δ 19%What your head gave up
Physical86 −8.7%
Cognitive82 −19.3%
Resilience84

The memo's numbers from its section 03, minus the Integration line that section 01 retires, laid out as a race result rather than a health report. The definition sits under the percentage, so the number teaches itself the first time somebody sees it, and the Δ gives the metric a mark that still reads at favicon size.

This is one state of three, and the other two decide everything. The card above is an athlete on session fourteen, with a personal best and a percentile behind them. The state that matters is the first one, with no plus-three, no comparison and no history, a bare number handed to somebody who has never seen one. That is the peak of their first visit and it is undesigned. The third is the session where the delta got worse, which decides whether a number becomes a habit or something people stop looking at.

Where to invest. These two assets score high on both things that matter: people will link them to the sport, and to nothing else. Every other visual decision gets judged by whether it makes these two more recognisable.

10 · The return

The second number is the business.

A brand proposal usually stops at the first visit. This one should not, because the sport has no product until somebody comes back, and at this stage retention is the only number worth watching. A curve that flattens rather than decaying to zero is the clearest signal any of this works. The club being a place people stay is half of that answer, and the number is the other half.

The delta is the reason to return, because a number somebody has been given is a number they want to move.

What accumulates

The hook

Mechanism: investment

Every session adds to a history that exists nowhere else. A year of delta curves is not portable to another gym, which makes leaving cost something, and that is what turns an unpredictable reward into a habit. The app is where that history lives, and the only reason the brand needs one.

The season

Commercial

Shape: baseline, twelve weeks, retest

Somebody arrives for the test and buys the retest. Selling the season rather than the class turns a one-off purchase into recurring revenue, and it follows from the metric rather than being bolted onto it.

Bring someone to compare with

The loop

Status: hypothesis, cheap to test

Nobody knows whether a 19% delta is good without another delta beside it. That comparison is the cheapest growth loop available and it costs nothing to build, because it is already how the number works.

The app, on screen

Four screens, and every one of them is the score card in a different state. The app has no other idea in it, which is what keeps it from looking like an app.

The seasonTwelve weeks, a retest date, and someone to compare with

Three rules the screens follow. The signal colour appears only where a measurement is happening or being shown, so the live pod, the Δ and the test marks are lime and nothing else is. Numbers are set in mono, large, and tabular, because the number is the product. And the practice screen says in its own words that it records nothing, because that is the rule that keeps the club worth paying for.

Where the peak is. People judge an experience by its peak and its ending rather than its average. The peak of a session is the moment somebody is handed their number, and that moment is undesigned. Whether it arrives on a wall, on a phone before they have left the room, or from a coach saying it out loud is a brand decision.

What transfers from benchmarks and what does not. Fitness sits among the habitual categories that hold retention above the cross-industry average, which helps, though those figures come from mobile apps and do not transfer to a box in Madrid. Two things do transfer. The shape rule, where a flattening curve beats any single number. And the Sean Ellis question, which works on twelve people as well as twelve thousand: how would you feel if you could no longer do this? Forty per cent answering “very disappointed” is the threshold, and it is measurable inside the four sessions already planned.

11 · The company session

The best team-building event is a test.

The standard Madrid offsite ends in an escape room or a paella, and neither produces a number. This does, about the one thing companies say they want from a team and have never been able to measure.

Companies say they want teams that decide well under pressure, and nobody has ever handed them a number for it.

Madrid already has corporate football leagues nobody writes about. A table where a law firm and a logistics company are ranked by how well they decide tired is where the community, the company money and the sport meet, once the format is licensed.

Leaves with a table, and a story a journalist writes unasked

What it does for the club

The company pays for the athlete's first visit.

A room of twenty from one company will contain a few of the person section 04 is built for, arriving with a first number in hand and the company's money behind it. That is the first visit paid for by somebody else, the cheapest acquisition this sport will ever have.

It also fills the weekday hours a club sells worst, and the weekend version carries the kit and the coaches wherever the company already booked, which makes it the demand map for the format. The first company asking whether its Barcelona office can do the same session has said where the next licensed room goes.

Off-peak hours filled · First visit paid by the employer · The licence pipeline, for free

Sold as the sport, and never as wellness. The buyer is a founder, a head of sales or a team lead who wants their people to decide better when it counts, a different person from the wellness buyer section 04 parks. Same vocabulary, same rules, same certified room, same recorded number. No lighter version for companies, because a diluted session produces a number that means nothing, and that is the end of the brand.

Whose number it is. A cognitive score inside an employment relationship is a sensitive thing, and the rule gets written before the first contract. The individual delta belongs to the individual, and the team gets only the team delta. Nobody's manager sees a person's number unless that person shows it. Put it in the contract and on the wall, because it is what makes the number something people trust.

The cost, and the one rule that contains it. Company money can pull a club toward the team-building shelf, next to the escape room it was meant to replace. Company sessions run off-peak and never displace an athlete, no logos go on the wall, and team names sit on the board in the sport's own type. The moment the room looks like a venue the athletes leave, and they are the reason the company came.

12 · What I would do next

Four things, then we look again.

Pick the name. Run the class 41 search on it and buy a domain you can defend. Rewrite the memo's first page around the belief rather than the science. Film forty-five seconds of a real session to sit beside the photographs.

With those four done I can bring you a wordmark, a lockup, the mark as it would sit on a licensee's wall, a one-page identity you could put in front of Nebrera, and the three states of the score card designed rather than sketched. Around ten days.

In the four pilot sessions, two things are worth counting because they cost nothing: how many second-visit athletes were brought by a first-visit athlete, and what people answer to the Sean Ellis question.

And the boring question before I start: if this moves, what is my role? Asking early because with Diago we left it to the end, and I would rather it be one sentence now.

des.

Strength you cannot use when it matters is decoration.
